intent: Answer “what can I cook with what I have?” with a practical method
title: What Can I Cook with These Ingredients? A Practical Guide
description: Stuck staring at the fridge? Use this practical method to decide what to cook with the ingredients you already have, and see how Delixio can generate meal ideas for you.
h1: What can I cook with these ingredients?
intro: When people ask “what can I cook with these ingredients?”, they usually have a short list: half a zucchini, some eggs, rice, a lonely chicken breast, or yesterday’s roast vegetables. The goal is not a perfect cookbook meal. The goal is a tasty dinner without another trip to the store.

Start by naming your constraints, time, servings, and how willing you are to buy missing items, then match your ingredients to a cooking format. Delixio can do this automatically once you enter what you have.

sections.heading: Ask four questions first
list: How much time do I have?
How many people am I cooking for?
What must be used soon (leftovers or produce that will not last)?
Am I cooking only with what I have, or can I add one small missing item?
paragraphs: Those answers prevent endless scrolling through recipes that do not fit your fridge or your evening.

sections.heading: Match ingredients to a meal format
paragraphs: Once you know your ingredients, pick a format that can absorb leftovers well:

examples.title: Skillet / stir-fry
examples.text: Best for mixed vegetables, leftover meat, eggs, tofu, or cooked rice.

examples.title: Soup or stew
examples.text: Best when you have odds and ends of vegetables, beans, or leftover roast.

examples.title: Pasta or noodles
examples.text: Best when you have a sauce base (tomatoes, cream, pesto, garlic-oil) plus a few add-ins.

examples.title: Bowl or salad
examples.text: Best for cooked grains, greens, beans, cheese, and leftover protein.

examples.title: Eggs for dinner
examples.text: Best when the fridge looks empty but you still have eggs, cheese, and a vegetable.

sections.heading: Example fridge lists and meal ideas

examples.title: Eggs, onion, cheese, tortillas
examples.text: Breakfast tacos or a folded omelette wrap with salsa if you have it.

examples.title: Cooked rice, frozen peas, eggs, soy sauce
Chicken, potatoes, mustard, herbs
examples.text: Roast or skillet chicken with mustard potatoes.

examples.title: Canned beans, tomatoes, spices, rice
examples.text: Bean stew over rice with whatever vegetables are left.

delixio.heading: Let Delixio answer from your real fridge
paragraphs: Open Delixio, type the ingredients you want to use, choose servings, cooking time, meal type, and Strict / Flexible / Creative mode, then generate free recipe ideas.

Unlock a full recipe when you are ready to cook (1 credit, with 1 free full recipe per day). If something is missing, add ingredients to your grocery list. You can also save recipes, rate them, add notes, mark them cooked, and schedule meals.

faq.q: What if I only have a few ingredients?
faq.a: Focus on one format that stretches food: eggs, pasta, rice bowls, soups, and skillet meals are usually the most forgiving.

faq.q: Should I include spices and oil in my list?
faq.a: Yes if they matter for flavor. Even a short list of garlic, lemon, chili, soy sauce, or herbs can change the meal.

faq.q: How does Delixio help with this question?
faq.a: You enter the ingredients you have and Delixio generates personalized recipe ideas around them. You can unlock full recipes with credits and add missing ingredients to a grocery list.

faq.q: Can I avoid ingredients I dislike?
faq.a: Yes. In Delixio, disliked ingredients are treated as hard excludes during generation, and you can also set diet preferences.

card_blurb: A simple method for fridge-first dinner decisions.
